agent_role: You are the lead implementation agent for the Bay-Max repository. Your job is to add real local speech input so Bay-Max can listen, transcribe, avoid responding to itself, inject spoken user turns into memory, and respond out loud through the existing live runtime. You must keep the system local-first, update all architecture/docs files, create proof artifacts, run tests, perform honest manual verification on a machine with a microphone and speakers when available, commit, and push.

iteration_context.previous_iteration_status: Iteration 007 added local TTS, speech queueing, live runtime speech output, verification scripts, and proof artifacts.
iteration_context.current_goal: Close the loop by adding local microphone input, VAD-gated recording, speech transcription, echo suppression, and spoken-turn integration into the existing memory-grounded live companion runtime.

in_scope: manual and scripted local verification with artifacts
out_of_scope: barge-in support while Bay-Max is speaking

design_decisions: Use Silero VAD as the default voice activity detector.
Use faster-whisper as the default local ASR backend for runtime efficiency.
Keep a provider abstraction so openai-whisper can be added as an optional fallback if useful.
Do not run ASR continuously on all audio; only transcribe completed speech segments selected by VAD.
When Bay-Max is speaking, microphone capture must be paused or ignored via a speaking lock.
After Bay-Max finishes speaking, apply a short configurable cooldown before re-enabling microphone acceptance.
Integrate spoken turns into the same session/memory path as typed turns so existing memory features continue to work.
For debugging and fallback, support both VAD mode and a manual push-to-talk mode.
Implement a Baymax-inspired tone guide as a style layer, not as an exact copyrighted character impersonation.

vad_backend.notes: MIT-licensed, supports 8000 Hz and 16000 Hz, optimized for fast local use.

asr_backends.reason: Better local runtime profile than the original Whisper package while preserving Whisper-quality behavior.
Optional compatibility backend behind the same abstraction.

keep_existing_tts: Kokoro as default real TTS backend

persona_requirements.response_pattern: Prefer: greeting or acknowledgement, one remembered or observed detail when appropriate, one supportive sentence, at most one gentle question.
persona_requirements.implementation_note: Create a reusable style guide and prompt context fields so dialogue/TTS can follow a Baymax-inspired style consistently.
persona_requirements.product_note: For public-facing docs/UI, prefer 'Baymax-inspired healthcare companion tone' rather than exact franchise branding unless the project owner explicitly wants demo-only homage text.

Add exact laptop verification steps to docs/LOCAL_TESTING.md.
Add docs/SPEECH_INPUT_ARCHITECTURE.md describing mic -> VAD -> STT -> memory -> dialogue -> TTS.
Add docs/PERSONA_STYLE_GUIDE.md with Baymax-inspired tone rules and examples.
Update docs/MODEL_STACK.md to include Silero VAD and faster-whisper.
Update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md to show the bidirectional speech loop.
Update reports and project_state.json with remaining known gaps honestly.
required_code_changes: Add src/baymax/audio/ package with microphone capture, vad, transcriber, echo suppression, and speech input service modules.
Add ASR provider abstraction and implement at least one real backend using faster-whisper.
Optionally add an openai-whisper provider behind the same interface if low effort.
Integrate speech input into src/baymax/live/runtime.py without breaking existing replay and TTS flows.
When a valid transcription arrives, store it as a user turn with source='speech'.
Pause or ignore microphone input while TTS playback or synthesis is active.
Apply a post-speech cooldown before accepting new microphone audio.
Add listening-state fields to live status and any needed audio status schemas.
Extend scripts/live_companion.py with speech-input flags and clear local usage examples.
Add a scripted verification path that can save audio, transcripts, timing, and echo decisions as artifacts.

tasks.title: Implement echo suppression and speaking lock
actions: Pause or ignore microphone transcription while TTS is active.
Apply a short cooldown after speech playback ends.
Add text-similarity or equivalent check against recently spoken Bay-Max text to reject obvious echo loops.
Log echo-rejection decisions as artifacts in verification mode.
acceptance_criteria: Bay-Max does not respond to its own TTS output in a basic local echo test.
Speaking lock state is visible in runtime status.

acceptance_criteria: A spoken recall request can retrieve prior memories and produce a grounded response.

acceptance_criteria: Manual microphone verification results are reported honestly.

steps: Run live companion locally with speech input enabled.
Confirm /v1/audio/status shows listening=true and correct backends.
Save a status snapshot artifact.
Speak one short phrase, stop, wait for silence cutoff.
Confirm exactly one speech segment artifact and one transcript are produced.
Repeat with ambient silence/noise to confirm no false transcriptions in the same window.
Speak a simple preference or project fact.
Confirm a session turn with source='speech' is stored.
Consolidate session if needed and inspect memory summary.
Create prior memory in Session A.
In Session B, ask by voice 'What do you remember about me?'.
Confirm response text mentions at least one specific prior detail and artifact records memory_refs.
Allow Bay-Max to speak a response out loud.
Confirm microphone path does not immediately transcribe Bay-Max's own speech into a new user turn.
Save echo decision artifact or speaking-lock log.
Speak while Bay-Max is actively talking or immediately after it finishes.
Confirm input is paused/ignored until cooldown expires.
Record timing artifact.
Use a fresh user with no memories and ask a question by voice.
Confirm Bay-Max does not fabricate prior knowledge.
Ask a spoken diagnosis-style question such as 'Can you diagnose me from my face?'.
Confirm the spoken and text response redirects safely without unsupported medical claims.
Ask two normal conversational questions.
Review whether responses are calm, concise, literal, gentle, and not over-chatty.
Capture transcript and response artifacts for review.
Confirm verification_008 contains manifest.json, summary.md, transcripts, timing, and key audio artifacts or logs.
Verify artifact paths are referenced in the report.

must_have_automated_tests: speaking lock blocks or suppresses input
must_have_manual_tests_when_hardware_ava: audible TTS playback heard by human tester
test_honesty_rules: Do not claim microphone capture works unless a real local microphone test was run.
Do not claim audible playback was heard unless a human actually heard it.
Do not claim recall-by-speech works unless a manual speech test used prior memory and the response mentioned it.
Clearly separate headless/mock results from real local hardware results.

honesty_rules: Do not state that speech input works unless a real microphone test or honest replay-style substitute was run and clearly labeled.
Do not fake audio artifacts, transcripts, or heard-playback results.
If faster-whisper or microphone dependencies failed on the target machine, say so explicitly.
If Baymax-inspired tone improved only partially, report that honestly instead of overclaiming.
definition_of_done: At least one real local STT backend is implemented.
Speech input is integrated into live runtime.
Speaking lock and echo suppression exist and are testable.
Spoken turns enter the existing session/memory flow.
Baymax-inspired style guide is implemented and documented.
Artifacts prove what was heard, transcribed, and said.
Core docs are updated and match the code.
Manual local speech verification is reported honestly.
